info.desc: Temple of the Dog is the only studio album by the American rock band Temple of the Dog, released on April 16, 1991 through A&M Records. The album is a tribute to Andrew Wood, the former lead singer of Malfunkshun and Mother Love Bone. Wood died on March 19, 1990 of a heroin overdose. The album has been certified platinum by the RIAA in the United States. Soundgarden frontman Chris Cornell, who had been Mother Love Bone vocalist Andrew Wood's roommate, approached former Mother Love Bone members Stone Gossard and Jeff Ament about working on material he had written when .

podcast.body: This "monstrously important record" was created in 1990 by surviving members of Mother Love Bone (Jeff Ament, Stone Gossard) and friends from Soundgarden, along with other local musicians, as a tribute to Mother Love Bone's deceased singer, Andrew Wood. The positive camaraderie during these sessions ultimately led to the formation of Pearl Jam. "Temple of the Dog and Hunger Strike from their one and only album from 1990. Monstrously important record."

podcast.body: A tribute album recorded by friends of Andrew Wood after his death. The project featured Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron from Soundgarden, former Mother Love Bone members Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard, Jeff McCready, and Eddie Vedder, retrospectively forming a Seattle Grunge Supergroup with members of Soundgarden and future Pearl Jam. "They call this project Temple of the Dog."

podcast.body: This album was recorded in just 15 days and released on April 16, 1991, as a tribute to Andrew Wood, the deceased singer of Mother Love Bone. It featured Chris Cornell, Matt Cameron, Jeff Ament, Stone Gossard, Mike McCready, and an unproven Eddie Vedder. Although it initially received great reviews but little attention, it later went multi-platinum worldwide after Soundgarden and Pearl Jam achieved massive success. "The Temple of the Dog album was recorded in just 15 days and released on April 16, 1991."

podcast.body: This self-titled, one-off album was a "tiny side project" formed in 1991 by members of Pearl Jam and Soundgarden as a tribute to the late Mother Love Bone frontman Andrew Wood. By late summer 1992, it broke into the top 10 of the album chart and belatedly went platinum, notably generating a top 10 hit, "Hunger Strike." "Temple of the Dog, a tribute to Andrew Wood, the late frontman of Mother Lovebone, broke into the top 10 on the album chart and went belatedly platinum."
